title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
會試錄序
禮部尚書臣濙左侍郎臣英以正
統十三年天下貢士就試京師者
循例奏請于
朝
皇上命臣穀臣寧為考官臣璉臣珵臣綸
臣恢臣曰讓臣勳臣賓臣輔則分考
===
焉監察御史臣澄臣圭寔防範之
暨內外各執事供莅惟謹于時預
試者凡千三百人得文字優粹者
百五十人小錄既成咸謂不可以
無序臣惟自古君天下者必藉賢
才以為之輔賢才之生匪得
朝廷作養造就簡拔而登用焉則藝

焉監察御史〔臣〕〔澄〕〔臣〕〔圭〕寔防範之
暨内外各執事供莅惟謹于時預
試者凡千三百人得文字優粹者
百五十人小録既成咸謂不可以
無序〔臣〕惟自古君天下者必藉賢
才以爲之輔賢才之生匪得
朝廷作養造就簡拔而登用焉則藝
punctuated:
會試錄序

禮部尚書臣濙、左侍郎臣英，以正統十三年天下貢士就試京師者，循例奏請于朝。皇上命臣穀、臣寧為考官，臣璉、臣珵、臣綸、臣恢、臣曰讓、臣勳、臣賓、臣輔則分考焉。監察御史臣澄、臣圭寔防範之，暨內外各執事供莅惟謹。于時預試者凡千三百人，得文字優粹者百五十人。小錄既成，咸謂不可以無序。

臣惟自古君天下者，必藉賢才以為之輔；賢才之生，匪得朝廷作養造就，簡拔而登用焉，則藝
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Metropolitan Examination

In the thirteenth year of the Zhengtong reign (1448), as the tribute scholars from across the realm gathered in the capital to sit for the examination, Your Servant [Hu] Ying 胡濙, Minister of Rites, and Your Servant [Chen] Ying 陳英, Left Vice Minister, petitioned the court in accordance with precedent. His Majesty commanded Your Servant [Chen] Xun 陳循 [Gu 穀?] and Your Servant [Gao] Gu 高穀 [Ning 寧?] to serve as Examiners, while Your Servant Lian 璉, Your Servant Cheng 珵, Your Servant Lun 綸, Your Servant Hui 恢, Your Servant Yuerang 曰讓, Your Servant Xun 勳, Your Servant Bin 賓, and Your Servant Fu 輔 divided the duties of Associate Examiners. Investigating Censors Your Servant Cheng 澄 and Your Servant Gui 圭 were charged with maintaining surveillance and precautions, and all the officiating functionaries inside and outside the compound attended to their duties with utmost care. At this time, those participating in the examination numbered one thousand three hundred in all, from whom one hundred and fifty whose compositions were of superior and pure quality were selected. Now that the petty record of the examination has been compiled, all say that it must not lack a preface.

Your Servant reflects that since antiquity, those who rule over All under Heaven have invariably relied upon worthy talents to assist them; yet when worthy talents are born, if they do not receive the nurturing and cultivation of the imperial court, and are not selected and elevated for employment, then by what means could their arts…

title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
何由而成身何由而進哉譬若滄
海有珠深林有木雖含精雨露凝
輝日月潤滋培植積歲既久其光
彩鬱秀固自若也及其見採于匠
石之手隨其器之大小高下別而
用之然後珠在淵木在山無沈晦
遺棄之惜以之為冠冕為佩玉為
===
棟梁為椽杙奚所往而不可得非
物之有合哉我
國家承平八十餘載休養生息既庶
且富人才之興超越前古其取士
之方雖不專乎一途然而得人之
效莫逾於科目盖科目之士沐教
養之

彩鬱秀固自若也及其見採于匠

用之然後珠在淵木在山無沈晦
遺棄之惜以之爲冠冕爲佩玉爲
===
棟梁爲榱杙奚所往而不可得非
物之有合哉我
國家承平八十餘載休養生息既庶
且富人才之興超越前古其取士
之方雖不界乎一途然而得人之
效莫逾於科目盖科目之士沐教
養之
punctuated: 何由而成？身何由而進哉？譬若滄海有珠，深林有木，雖含精雨露，凝輝日月，潤滋培植，積歲既久，其光彩鬱秀，固自若也；及其見採于匠石之手，隨其器之大小高下，別而用之，然後珠在淵、木在山，無沈晦遺棄之惜。以之為冠冕、為佩玉、為棟梁、為椽杙，奚所往而不可？得非物之有合哉？我國家承平八十餘載，休養生息，既庶且富，人才之興，超越前古。其取士之方，雖不專乎一途，然而得人之效，莫逾於科目。盖科目之士，沐教養之
translation_en:
… how could their skills be brought to completion, and how could their persons advance? It is like pearls in the vast sea or timber in the deep forest: although they absorb the essence of rain and dew and gather the radiance of sun and moon, being nourished and cultivated over the long accumulation of years so that their luster and luxuriant beauty are naturally self-possessed, it is only when they are gathered by the hands of a master craftsman, who distinguishes and employs them according to the size and grade of the vessel or structure, that the pearls in the depths and the timber in the mountains are spared the regret of sinking into obscurity and being cast aside. Whether fashioned into ceremonial caps and crowns or jade pendants, or into ridgepoles and beams or rafters and posts, where might they be put to use and not prove suitable? Is this not because things find their proper match?

Our Dynasty has enjoyed peace for more than eighty years, nurturing and giving rest to the people so that they are both numerous and prosperous, and the flourishing of men of talent surpasses that of all antiquity. Although its methods of selecting scholars are not confined to a single path, in the efficacy of obtaining capable men nothing surpasses the civil service examination curriculum. For the scholars of the examination curriculum, bathed in the [grace] of instruction and nurture …

title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
恩泳道德之化朝經暮史日就月將以
明體適用之學欲致其君以竭誠
殫力之才欲澤夫民由是出而任
斯理者炳炳琅琅措諸事業容或
可觀斯皆
朝廷平素教養之所致諸士子今日
之所以遭際明盛固榮且幸矣由
===
兹以進尚當以科目自重期副乎
朝廷所選擇立心行己揚名顯親與
古之賢達者相為後先庶可謂不
負
國恩不負所學焉是為序
嘉議大夫工部右侍郎兼翰林院
侍講學士

古之賢達者相為後先庶可謂不

嘉議大夫工部右侍郎兼翰林院
侍講學士
punctuated:
恩，泳道德之化，朝經暮史，日就月將，以明體適用之學，欲致其君；以竭誠殫力之才，欲澤夫民。由是出而任斯理者，炳炳琅琅，措諸事業，容或可觀，斯皆朝廷平素教養之所致。諸士子今日之所以遭際明盛，固榮且幸矣。由兹以進，尚當以科目自重，期副乎朝廷所選擇，立心行己，揚名顯親，與古之賢達者相為後先，庶可謂不負國恩，不負所學焉。是為序。
嘉議大夫、工部右侍郎兼翰林院侍講學士
translation_en:
…grace and swim in the transformative influence of morality and virtue. Studying the Classics in the morning and the histories in the evening, making daily and monthly progress, with learning that illuminates fundamental principles and applies them to practical use, they wish to devote themselves to their sovereign; with talents committed to exhausting their sincerity and strength, they wish to bring benefit to the people. Those who emerge from this path to take up the responsibilities of governance are brilliant and illustrious, and when they put their learning into practice in public undertakings, their achievements may well be worthy of admiration. All of this is brought about by the court's habitual instruction and nurturing. That you scholars today have encountered such an enlightened and flourishing age is truly both an honor and good fortune. Advancing from here, you should all the more hold yourselves in high esteem as men selected through the examination system, hoping to live up to the court's selection. In establishing your minds and conducting yourselves, and in making your names renowned to bring glory to your parents, may you rival in succession the worthies and eminent men of antiquity; only then can it be said that you have neither failed the grace of the dynasty nor failed what you have learned. This serves as the preface.

Grand Master for Splendid Discussion, Right Vice Minister of Works concurrently Expositor-in-Waiting in the Hanlin Academy…

translation_en:
Metropolitan Examination of the Thirteenth Year of the Zhengtong Era (1448)

Administrators of the Examination (知貢舉官)
Hu Ying 胡濙, Grand Master for Assisting toward Virtue, Senior Worthy of Rectified Governance, and Minister of Rites (courtesy name Yuanjie 源潔, a native of Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture; metropolitan graduate of the gengchen year [1400]).
Wang Ying 王英, Grand Master for Proper Consultation, Governor of Assisting Governance, and Left Vice Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-waiting (courtesy name Shiyan 時彥, a native of Jinxi County, Jiangxi; metropolitan graduate of the jiashen year [1404]).

Examiners (考試官)
Gao Gu 高穀, Grand Master for Splendid Advice and Right Vice Minister of Works concurrently serving as Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-waiting (courtesy name Shiyong 世用, a native of Xinghua County, Yangzhou Prefecture; metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year [1415]).
Du Ning 杜寧, Expositor-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Fostering Virtue (courtesy name Zongmi 宗謐, a native of Tiantai County, Zhejiang; metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year [1427]).

Associate Examiners (同考試官)
Xie Lian 謝璉, Expositor-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Fostering Honesty (courtesy name Zhongqi 重器, a native of Longxi County, Fujian; metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year [1427]).
Xu Cheng 徐珵, Expositor-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Fostering Honesty (courtesy name Yuanyu 元玉, a native of Wu County, Southern Metropolitan Area [Zhili]; metropolitan graduate of the guichou year [1433]).
Pei Lun 裴綸, Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman of the Confucian Forest (courtesy name Jingxuan 景宣, a native of Jianli County, Huguang; metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year [1421]).
Zhao Hui 趙恢, Junior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman-litterateur (courtesy name Ruhong 汝弘, a native of Lianjiang County, Fujian; metropolitan graduate of the guichou year [1433]).
Sun Yuerang 孫曰讓, Instructor of the Prefectural Confucian School of Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang (a native of Fengcheng County, Jiangxi; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the gengzi year [1420]).
Lin Qin 林勤, Instructor of the County Confucian School of Fengxin County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi (courtesy name Keguang 克廣, a native of Putian County, Fujian; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the jiawu year [1414]).
Chen Bin 陳賓, Instructor of the County Confucian School of Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (courtesy name Weiyin 惟寅, a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the dingyou year [1417]).
Jiang Fu 蔣輔, Assistant Instructor of the County Confucian School of Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi (courtesy name Tingzuo 廷佐, a native of Longyan County, Fujian; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the jiyou year [1429]).

Monitoring Officials (監試官)
Wang Cheng 汪澄, Gentleman-litterateur and Investigating Censor of the Fujian Circuit (courtesy name Shiyuan 士淵, a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the bingwu year [1426]).

title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
才難不其然乎唐虞之際於斯為盛
耕也餒在其中矣學也禄在其中矣
今夫天斯昭昭之多及其無窮也日月星辰繫焉
萬物覆焉今夫地一撮土之多及其廣厚載
華嶽而不重振河海而不洩萬物載焉今夫山
一卷石之多及其廣大草木生之禽獸居之寶
藏興焉今夫水一勺之多及其不測黿鼉蛟
===
龍魚鼈生焉貨財殖焉
易
象曰大人之吉位正當也
益動而巽日進无疆天施地生其益无方凡益之
道與時偕行
剛柔者立本者也變通者趣時者也吉凶者貞勝
者也天地之道貞觀者也日月之道貞明者也
天下之動貞夫一者也
天地設位聖人成能川

藏興焉今夫水一勺之多及其不測黿鼉蛟
龍魚鼈生焉貨財殖焉
===
易
象曰大人之吉位正當也
益動而巽日進无疆天施地生其益无方凡益之
道與時偕行
剛柔者立本者也變通者趣時者也吉凶者貞勝
者也天地之道貞觀者也日月之道貞明者也
天下之動貞夫一者也
天地設位聖人成能
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「才難」，不其然乎？唐、虞之際，於斯為盛。
耕也，餒在其中矣；學也，禄在其中矣。
今夫天，斯昭昭之多；及其無窮也，日月星辰繫焉，萬物覆焉。今夫地，一撮土之多；及其廣厚，載華嶽而不重，振河海而不洩，萬物載焉。今夫山，一卷石之多；及其廣大，草木生之，禽獸居之，寶藏興焉。今夫水，一勺之多；及其不測，黿、鼉、蛟、龍、魚、鼈生焉，貨財殖焉。

易
《象》曰：「大人之吉」，位正當也。
《益》，動而巽，日進无疆。天施地生，其益无方。凡益之道，與時偕行。
剛柔者，立本者也；變通者，趣時者也。吉凶者，貞勝者也；天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明者也；天下之動，貞夫一者也。
天地設位，聖人成能川。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
1. "'Talent is hard to find'—is this not truly so? Between the ages of Tang and Yu, it was at this time that talent flourished most." (Analects 8.20)
2. "In farming, hunger may be found therein; in learning, official emolument may be found therein." (Analects 15.32)
3. "Now as for heaven, it is at first no more than this patch of brightness; yet when we come to its boundlessness, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations are suspended in it, and all things are overspread by it. Now as for earth, it is at first no more than a pinch of soil; yet when we come to its breadth and thickness, it supports Mount Hua without feeling its weight, contains the rivers and seas without letting them leak away, and bears all things upon it. Now as for a mountain, it is at first no more than a fistful of rock; yet when we come to its vastness, grasses and trees grow upon it, birds and beasts dwell on it, and precious treasures arise within it. Now as for water, it is at first no more than a ladleful; yet when we come to its unfathomable depths, giant sea turtles, alligators, flood-dragons, dragons, fishes, and soft-shelled turtles are born in it, and goods and wealth multiply within it." (Doctrine of the Mean 26)

Classic of Changes (Yijing)
1. "The Commentary on the Images says: 'The good fortune of the great man' is because his position is correct and appropriate." (Hexagram 12, Pi)
2. "Increase (Yi): movement and compliance, advancing daily without bound. Heaven bestows and earth brings forth; its increase knows no limit. Every way of increase proceeds in step with the times." (Hexagram 42, Yi, Commentary on the Judgments)
3. "The firm and the yielding are what establish the foundation; change and continuity are what move with the times. Good fortune and misfortune are what prevail through constancy; the way of heaven and earth is what is manifest through constancy; the way of sun and moon is what shines through constancy; all movements under heaven are held constant by the One." (Great Commentary, Part II.1)
4. "Heaven and earth fix their positions, and the sage fulfills their capabilities [?]." (Great Commentary, Part II.12)

公既定宅伻来来視予卜休恒吉我二人共貞公其

其惟克用常人

吉蠲為饎是用孝享禴祠烝嘗于公先王君曰卜

punctuated:
書
三載考績，三考黜陟幽明，庶績咸熈，分北三苗。
以厥庶民暨厥臣，達大家；以厥臣達王，惟邦君。
公既定宅，伻来，来視予卜休恒吉。我二人共貞，公其以予萬億年敬天之休。
其惟克用常人。

詩
吉蠲為饎，是用孝享。禴祠烝嘗，于公先王。君曰卜尔，萬壽無疆。神之弔矣，詒尔多福。民之質矣，日用飲食。群黎百姓，徧為尔德。
戎車既安，如輊如軒。四牡既佶，既佶且閑。薄伐玁狁，至于大原。文武吉甫，萬邦為憲。
亹亹文王，令聞不已。陳錫哉周，侯文王孫子。文王孫子，本支百世。凡周之士，不顯亦世。
自今以始，歲其有。君子有穀，詒孫子，于胥樂兮。

春秋
齊侯、鄭伯盟于石門〔隱三〕；宋公、齊侯、衛侯盟于瓦屋〔隱八〕；會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許
translation_en:
Book of Documents (Shu):
"Every three years there was an examination of merits, and after three examinations the undeserving were degraded and the deserving promoted. Thus all official achievements were resplendent, and the Sanmiao were separated and isolated."
"It is the ruler of a state who connects his common people and his ministers with the great families, and who connects his ministers with the king."
"Now that the Duke has settled the site, he sent a messenger to come and show me the auspicious and ever-favorable divinations. May the two of us jointly bear the responsibility; may the Duke with me for myriads and hundreds of thousands of years revere the grace of Heaven."
"It is only when he is able to employ men of constant virtue."

Book of Odes (Shi):
"Auspicious and pure are the sacrificial meats, with which you make filial offerings; in spring, summer, autumn, and winter sacrifices, to the Dukes and Former Kings. The deceased rulers say: 'We grant you a myriad years of life without bound.' The spirits arrive and bestow upon you manifold blessings. The people are simple and honest, daily taking their drink and food; theblack-haired multitudes of all the clans universally practice your virtue."
"The war chariots were well balanced, as if tilted forward, as if tilted back; the four stallions were strong, both strong and well-trained. We attacked the Xianyun as far as Taiyuan; civil and martial is Jifu, a model to all the states."
"Tireless was King Wen, his good fame never ends. He spread his gifts over Zhou, down to the grandsons and sons of King Wen. The grandsons and sons of King Wen, root and branch for a hundred generations; and all the officers of Zhou, are they not illustrious too from generation to generation?"
"From now on, may the years be abundant. The lord has grain to leave to his grandsons and sons—oh, let us all rejoice together!"

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The two books imperially composed by Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor [the Yongle Emperor], Secret Merits of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Deeds of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), were intended to encourage people to do good and to rouse their hearts to love their parents; their benefit to the moral instruction of the world is great indeed! Yet among secret merits, none takes precedence over benevolence and generosity; and among filial deeds, none is more difficult than moving others and nature through sincerity. Among the ancients, some disputed legal cases with their governors, some wept while sentencing prisoners, some rescued others and were consequently dismissed from office, and some upheld rectitude without pandering; there were those renowned for leaving no grievances unredressed, and those who received karmic rewards for their meticulous care in judgment; there were those who tirelessly redressed the cases of the mistakenly implicated, and those whose benevolence and leniency resembled Zhang Shizhi 張釋之—can all these individuals be named and cited? On a grand scale, moving heaven and earth and stirring ghosts and spirits brought the effects of calming winds, summoning rain, halting hail, and extinguishing fires; on a subtle scale, transforming the violent, moving birds and beasts, and instilling trust even in grasses and trees brought the responses of touching the hearts of bandits to preserve people from disaster and the auspicious signs of numinous fungi and extraordinary trees—can these deeds also be recounted? Set them forth one by one.

以告之歟？夫律呂有三統之義，以配十二月。其陰陽取類之義，損益相生之法，正變全半之辨，分寸度數之詳，可得言歟？近代西山蔡氏作《律呂新書》，子朱子稱其「深沉縝密，明白通暢」，其法亦有合於古歟？太史公敘《律書》，其始不言律而言兵，或者謂知製律之本。所謂本者，果何在歟？願悉陳之，毋畧。

問：昔之為治者，自三代以後，必先兩漢焉。西漢由高祖得天下，其所以與共理者，率多刀筆吏，儒者僅一二見焉。當時蕭、曹功業最盛，叔孫通以文學定禮儀，其功業不能與之抗衡，何歟？逮至文、景，治比成、康，論者謂所尚皆黃老之術；孝武繼業，儒者公孫弘之徒用事，論者謂治效不及乎文、景；宣帝中興，侔德商宗、周宣，然所用多刑名法理之士。漢之風俗治道號為淳美，果刀筆、清淨所致乎？抑
translation_en:
…to tell him? Now, the yang and yin pitch-pipes (lülü) embody the principle of the Three Sequences (santong), matching the twelve months. Can you discuss the principle of their categorization according to yin and yang, the method of their mutual generation through subtraction and addition, the distinction between regular and altered, whole and half pitches, and the details of their measurements in tenths of an inch (fen), inches (cun), and degrees? In recent times, Master Cai of Xishan (Cai Yuanding 蔡元定) composed the New Treatise on the Pitch-Pipes (Lülü xinshu), which Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) praised as "profound and meticulous, clear and fluent." Does his method indeed accord with antiquity? When the Grand Historian (Sima Qian 司馬遷) composed the "Treatise on the Pitch-Pipes" (Lüshu), at the beginning he did not speak of pitch-pipes, but spoke of military affairs; some say he understood the fundamental basis of making pitch-pipes. Wherein does this so-called fundamental basis actually lie? Please set this forth in full, without omission.

Question: Among those who achieved good governance in the past, after the Three Dynasties, the Two Han dynasties are always placed first. After Emperor Gaozu (高祖) won the realm in the Western Han, those with whom he jointly governed were mostly minor clerks of the knife and brush (daobili), while Confucian scholars were seen in only one or two instances. At that time, the meritorious achievements of Xiao He (蕭何) and Cao Shen (曹參) were the most flourishing; Shusun Tong (叔孫通) established court rituals and etiquette through his literary learning, yet his achievements could not rival theirs—why was this? Down to the reigns of Emperors Wen (文帝) and Jing (景帝), their governance was compared to that of Kings Cheng (成王) and Kang (康王) of Zhou, yet commentators say that what they esteemed were all the arts of Huang-Lao (the Yellow Emperor and Laozi). When the Filial Emperor Wu (孝武, Emperor Wu) succeeded to the enterprise, Confucian scholars such as Gongsun Hong (公孫弘) and his ilk held power, yet commentators say the efficacy of their governance did not match that of Emperors Wen and Jing. Emperor Xuan (宣帝) achieved a dynastic restoration, matching in virtue the high ancestors of Shang and King Xuan of Zhou (周宣王), yet those whom he employed were mostly men versed in criminal law and legal principles (xingming fali). The customs and way of governance of the Han were renowned as pure and admirable—was this really brought about by petty legal clerks and Daoist quietism (qingjing)? Or…

儒者有所經濟乎？盖為治必宗周、孔之教，斯乃無弊。周、孔之教，仁義之言是也。前乎既往，後乎方來，舉而行之，皆有明驗。諸君子平居以儒者自任，必有能發斯理者，幸言之毋隱。

問：乾象之說，所以明天道、謹人事，以正四時。自伏羲仰觀俯察以驗動靜，黃帝創受《河圖》以明休咎以來，未聞有其書也。厥後星官有紀，推測有法，往往出於占候者之手，其立意創制，昉於何代，備於何人歟？談天者類以巫咸、甘、石三數家為後世所宗，其為書果可以超絕後先歟？漢、唐名家者，有《靈憲》，有《法象志》，有《覆矩圖》，其言之詳畧、學之純駁，可以儕於巫咸、甘、石否歟？姑以一事論之：漢史載十月五星聚東井，至魏高允與崔浩議其非，謂金、水二星常附日而行，當冬十月時，日旦在尾、箕，昏沒於申南，而東井
translation_en:
… that the Confucian scholars contributed something to statecraft and administration? Indeed, governance must take the teachings of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius as its standard in order to be free of defects. The teachings of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius consist precisely in words of benevolence and righteousness. Looking back to the past and forward to the future, whenever these are taken up and put into practice, there is always clear proof of their efficacy. In your daily lives, you gentlemen take upon yourselves the responsibilities of Confucian scholars; surely you are able to elucidate this principle. Please speak of it without holding back.

Question: Theories of the celestial phenomena serve to illuminate the Way of Heaven, regulate human affairs with care, and rectify the four seasons. Since Fuxi looked up to contemplate the heavens and looked down to examine the earth in order to verify motion and stillness, and the Yellow Emperor first received the River Chart (Hetu) to clarify good and bad fortune, one does not hear of any books on the subject. Thereafter, astrological officials kept records and methods of calculation and prediction existed, often coming from the hands of diviners and sky-watchers. In what era did the formulation of these concepts and the creation of these systems begin, and by whom were they brought to completion? Those who discuss the heavens generally regard the three or so schools of Wu Xian, Gan De, and Shi Shen as the authorities followed by later generations; do their writings truly surpass all that came before and after? Among the renowned masters of the Han and Tang dynasties, there were the Spiritual Constitution of the Universe (Lingxian), the Treatise on Regularities and Phenomena (Faxiang zhi), and the Diagram of the Inverted Carpenter's Square (Fuju tu). In the thoroughness or brevity of their accounts and the purity or unevenness of their learning, can they be ranked alongside Wu Xian, Gan De, and Shi Shen, or not? Let us discuss just one matter: the Han histories record that in the tenth month the Five Planets gathered in the Eastern Well (Dongjing) lodge. Yet when it came to the Northern Wei, Gao Yun 高允 discussed the error of this with Cui Hao 崔浩, arguing that the two planets Venus and Mercury always travel in proximity to the sun, and that in the tenth month of winter, at dawn the sun is in the Tail (Wei) and Winnowing-Basket (Ji) lodges, sinking at dusk in the south-southwest (shen-nan), whereas the Eastern Well…

text:
方出於寅此二星何得背日而行其說
果當歟曆象授時儒者所當究請詳言
之以觀所蘊
alt_text:
方出於寅此二星何得背日而行其說
果當歟曆家授時儒者所當究請詳言
之以觀所蘊
punctuated: 方出於寅，此二星何得背日而行？其說果當歟？曆象授時，儒者所當究，請詳言之，以觀所蘊。
translation_en: …was just rising in the yin direction [east-northeast]. How could these two planets move away from the sun? Is this explanation indeed correct? Calendrical calculation, observation of celestial phenomena, and the promulgation of the seasons are matters that Confucian scholars ought to investigate. Please discuss them in detail, so that we may assess the learning you possess.

title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
四書
才難不其然乎唐虞之際於斯為盛
彭時
同考試官教授孫批此篇明白簡潔優於他
作宜在選列
考試官侍講杜批此題本平易而作者多不能
發越唯此篇暢達可喜佳作也
考試官學士高批此篇說周之人才不及唐虞
從容不迫之意於文辭見矣欣羨欣羨
===
聖人既述古語以見人才之難為可信復即聖世而
見人才之生盛於周盖人才之難得古今皆然也有
周之人才非不盛矣而唐虞之際乃盛於此聖人安
得不信古語而嘆之哉思昔聖人之意若曰才者德
之用也德極其盛則才無不全天之生才豈偶然哉
必真元之氣合而後一代之全才生焉其生也曠世
而始見必光岳之秀鍾而後一代之全才出焉其出
也間世而一覩然則古語所謂才難者豈不信矣哉
以有周之世觀之周召著夾輔之勳畢榮極賛襄之

四書

「才難，不其然乎？唐虞之際，於斯為盛。」

彭時

同考試官教授孫批：此篇明白簡潔，優於他作，宜在選列。

考試官侍講杜批：此題本平易，而作者多不能發越，唯此篇暢達可喜，佳作也。

考試官學士高批：此篇說周之人才不及唐虞，從容不迫之意於文辭見矣。欣羨！欣羨！

聖人既述古語以見人才之難為可信，復即聖世而見人才之生盛於周。盖人才之難得，古今皆然也。有周之人才非不盛矣，而唐虞之際乃盛於此，聖人安得不信古語而嘆之哉？思昔聖人之意，若曰：才者，德之用也。德極其盛，則才無不全。天之生才，豈偶然哉？必真元之氣合，而後一代之全才生焉，其生也曠世而始見；必光岳之秀鍾，而後一代之全才出焉，其出也間世而一覩。然則古語所謂才難者，豈不信矣哉？以有周之世觀之，周召著夾輔之勳，畢榮極賛襄之
translation_en:
Four Books

“Talent is hard to find—is this not so? At the juncture of Tang and Yu, it was more abundant than here.”

Peng Shi

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: This essay is clear and concise, superior to the other compositions, and deserves inclusion among the selections.

Comment by Examiner Du, Expositor-in-waiting: This topic is straightforward, yet most writers fail to bring out its full meaning. This essay alone expresses it freely and lucidly, to pleasing effect. It is an excellent composition.

Comment by Examiner Gao, Academician: This essay explains that the talented men of Zhou did not equal those of Tang and Yu. An easy, unhurried manner is evident in its language. How admirable! How admirable!

Having cited an ancient saying to show that the difficulty of finding talented men was indeed credible, the Sage then turned to an age of sage rule to show that talented men arose more abundantly then than under Zhou. For talent has always been difficult to obtain, in antiquity as in the present. Talented men were certainly abundant under Zhou, yet at the juncture of Tang and Yu—the reigns of Yao and Shun—they were still more abundant. How could the Sage fail to believe the ancient saying and sigh over it? Reflecting on what the Sage meant, we may imagine him saying: Talent is the functioning of virtue. When virtue reaches its fullest flourishing, talent is complete in every respect. Could Heaven’s production of talent be a matter of chance? Only when the true primordial vital energies unite does a person of comprehensive talent arise for an age; such a person appears only after a long succession of generations. Only when the finest essences of the heavenly luminaries and the great mountains gather does a person of comprehensive talent emerge for an age; such a person is seen only at intervals of generations. Is not the ancient saying that talent is hard to find therefore truly credible? Consider the age of Zhou: the Dukes of Zhou and Shao distinguished themselves through their meritorious support of the ruler, while Bi and Rong devoted their utmost efforts to assisting …

title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
力以至大顛閎夭之徒散宜生南宫适之輩莫不疏
附先後而有以佐國家於隆平之盛莫不奔走禦侮
而有以躋斯世於熈皥之域其才可謂盛矣然惟唐
虞之際乃盛於此焉盖唐虞交會之間堯舜以聖繼
聖人才以類而傑出禹之平水土稷之播百穀其視
夫周之十人豈不為尤盛哉契之敷教皐陶之明刑
伯益之烈山澤其視夫周之十人又豈不為尤盛哉
降自夏商皆不能及此人才之所以為難得也吁堯
舜以聖聖繼作而後禹皐聖賢之才出文武以聖聖
===
繼作而後周召聖賢之才生天地真元會合之運亘
古而僅兩見者也或疑唐虞五人不能盛於周室十
人者殊不知唐虞之才皆千人之俊萬人之傑也傳
曰三卿為主可謂衆矣其斯之謂歟
耕也餒在其中矣學也禄在其中矣
萬安
同考試官脩撰裴批此題是以君子謀道不謀食
一句統說中分兩股又恐人錯認教人謀道以求食
故下面又繳一句君子憂道不憂貧是篇得之非

…efforts, down to the likes of Dadian and Hong Yao, and such men as San Yisheng and Nangong Kuo—there were none who did not bring the distant near and lead from before and behind, thereby assisting the state in an era of flourishing peace; there were none who did not hasten about to ward off aggression, thereby raising this world to the realm of serene harmony. Their talents may indeed be called abundant! Yet only at the juncture of Tang and Yu were talents even more abundant than this. For during the transition between Tang and Yu, Yao and Shun succeeded sage with sage, and men of talent stood out heroically according to their kind. Yu's regulating of the waters and land, and Ji's sowing of the hundred grains—when compared to those ten men of Zhou, how could they not be even more abundant? Xie's propagating of instruction, Gao Yao's clarifying of punishments, and Bo Yi's burning off the growth of mountains and marshes—when compared to those ten men of Zhou, how, again, could they not be even more abundant? Coming down through the Xia and Shang dynasties, none could match this; this is why men of talent are so difficult to obtain. Ah! Only after Yao and Shun arose in succession as sage upon sage did the sagely and worthy talents of Yu and Gao Yao emerge; only after Kings Wen and Wu arose in succession as sage upon sage were the sagely and worthy talents of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao born. The destiny of the convergence of the true primordial vital force of Heaven and Earth has been seen only twice across all antiquity! Some might doubt that the five men of Tang and Yu could be more abundant than the ten men of the House of Zhou, not realizing at all that the talents of Tang and Yu were every one of them the finest among a thousand men, the heroes among ten thousand. The commentary says: "With three ministers as the mainstay, they may be called numerous." Is this not what is meant here?

title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
深於本領之學者不能
考試官侍講杜批理明詞暢可取
考試官學士高批此篇立論措辞皆可觀正之
以為冠
力於農者未必得其食力於學者自然得其禄盖耕
所以求食而學所以求道也求夫食者不期於餒而
餒在其中求夫道者不期於禄而禄自至聖人言此
其示人治其本而不卹其末之意有在矣且夫人之
服田也載芟載柞其耕澤澤而沾體塗足之不憚其
===
勞以我覃耜俶載南畝而徂隰徂畛之不辭其苦其
耕之力也如此無非欲望收成之多以資日用之食
豈不有意於求食哉然或水旱之所傷蟊螣之所害
黍稷重穋不得以實堅而實好禾麻菽麥不得以實
穎而實栗飢餒之來自有不期然而然矣雖然耕本
以求食而不期不得其食學本以求道而不期自得
夫禄且人之為學朝夕匪懈而格致誠正之功無一
而不盡慎思明辨而脩齊治平之理無一而不窮學
之力也如此亦惟明夫當然之道於吾心而已初豈

力於農者未必得其食，力於學者自然得其禄。盖耕所以求食，而學所以求道也。求夫食者不期於餒，而餒在其中；求夫道者不期於禄，而禄自至。聖人言此，其示人治其本而不卹其末之意有在矣。且夫人之服田也，載芟載柞，其耕澤澤，而沾體塗足之不憚其勞；以我覃耜，俶載南畝，而徂隰徂畛之不辭其苦。其耕之力也如此，無非欲望收成之多，以資日用之食，豈不有意於求食哉？然或水旱之所傷，蟊螣之所害，黍稷重穋不得以實堅而實好，禾麻菽麥不得以實穎而實栗，飢餒之來，自有不期然而然矣。雖然，耕本以求食，而不期不得其食；學本以求道，而不期自得夫禄。且人之為學，朝夕匪懈，而格致誠正之功無一而不盡；慎思明辨，而脩齊治平之理無一而不窮。學之力也如此，亦惟明夫當然之道於吾心而已，初豈

…one without profound learning in the fundamentals could not accomplish this.

Examiner Gao, Academician, comments: “Both the argument and the wording of this essay are admirable. Upon correction, I place it first [?].”

Those who exert themselves in farming do not necessarily obtain their food; those who exert themselves in learning naturally obtain their official emolument. Farming is the means of seeking food, whereas learning is the means of seeking the Way. Those seeking food do not expect hunger, yet hunger lies within their undertaking; those seeking the Way do not expect emolument, yet emolument comes of itself. In saying this, the Sage intended to teach people to attend to the root without worrying about its incidental consequences.

Consider those who work the fields: they cut the grass and clear the trees, plowing until the soil is loosened. They do not shrink from the toil of soaking their bodies and muddying their feet. With their sharp plowshares they begin work in the southern fields; they go to the lowlands and the field paths, refusing none of the hardship. Such is their exertion in farming. All of it is undertaken in hope of a plentiful harvest to provide their daily food. Do they not deliberately seek food? Yet floods or drought may damage the crops, and root-eating grubs and leaf-eating pests may harm them. The millets, both late-sown and early-ripening, cannot grow firm and fine; the grain, hemp, beans, and wheat cannot develop full ears and solid kernels. Hunger thus arrives of itself, an outcome they did not expect.

Nevertheless, farming is originally undertaken to seek food, yet unexpectedly one may fail to obtain it; learning is originally undertaken to seek the Way, yet unexpectedly one obtains emolument of itself. Consider those engaged in learning: diligent morning and evening, they fully apply themselves to investigating things, extending knowledge, making their intentions sincere, and rectifying their minds. Thinking carefully and distinguishing clearly, they thoroughly investigate the principles of cultivating themselves, regulating their families, governing the state, and bringing peace to the realm. Such is their exertion in learning. It is solely to illuminate in their own minds the Way of what ought to be done. How could they initially have intended…

有意於干祿哉殆見天爵既脩人爵自至非有心於
公卿大夫之爵也而公卿大夫之爵自不能舍之而
他往雖無意於千駟萬鍾之祿也而千駟萬鍾之祿
自不能舍之而他適是爵祿之來自有不期然而然
矣嗟夫君子之學為己之學也君子之心為己之心
也故其為學惟知謀道而已非有意於謀食惟知憂
道而已亦非有意於憂貧故上文既曰君子謀道不
謀食而下文復曰君子憂道不憂貧學者可不以聖
人之言為勉哉
===
今夫天斯昭昭之多及其無窮也日月星辰繫
焉萬物覆焉今夫地一撮土之多及其廣厚
載華嶽而不重振河海而不洩萬物載焉今
夫山一卷石之多及其廣大草木生之禽獸
居之寶藏興焉今夫水一勺之多及其不測
黿鼉蛟龍魚鼈生焉貨財殖焉

有意於干祿哉？殆見天爵既脩，人爵自至，非有心於公卿大夫之爵也，而公卿大夫之爵自不能舍之而他往；雖無意於千駟萬鍾之祿也，而千駟萬鍾之祿自不能舍之而他適。是爵祿之來，自有不期然而然矣。嗟夫！君子之學，為己之學也；君子之心，為己之心也。故其為學，惟知謀道而已，非有意於謀食；惟知憂道而已，亦非有意於憂貧。故上文既曰：「君子謀道不謀食。」而下文復曰：「君子憂道不憂貧。」學者可不以聖人之言為勉哉？

今夫天，斯昭昭之多，及其無窮也，日月星辰繫焉，萬物覆焉。今夫地，一撮土之多，及其廣厚，載華嶽而不重，振河海而不洩，萬物載焉。今夫山，一卷石之多，及其廣大，草木生之，禽獸居之，寶藏興焉。今夫水，一勺之多，及其不測，黿鼉蛟龍魚鼈生焉，貨財殖焉。

translation_en:
…have any intention of seeking official emoluments? We see that once the nobility conferred by Heaven has been cultivated, humanly conferred nobility comes of itself. One has no deliberate desire for the ranks of dukes, ministers, and grandees, yet those ranks cannot pass one by and go elsewhere. Though one has no desire for the emoluments of a thousand teams of four horses and ten thousand measures of grain, those emoluments cannot pass one by and go to another. Thus rank and emolument arrive unexpectedly, of their own accord. Ah! The gentleman’s learning is learning for his own moral improvement; his heart is set on his own moral improvement. Hence, in learning, he knows only to seek the Way, without intending to seek sustenance; he knows only to be concerned about the Way, without intending to be concerned about poverty. Thus the preceding passage says, “The gentleman seeks the Way, not sustenance,” and the following passage says again, “The gentleman is concerned about the Way, not poverty.” Can students fail to take the sage’s words as an exhortation?

“Now Heaven is but this small expanse of brightness; yet in its infinity, the sun, moon, and stars are suspended in it, and all things are sheltered beneath it. Now Earth is but a pinch of soil; yet in its breadth and depth, it bears Mount Hua without finding it heavy, contains the rivers and seas without letting them leak away, and carries all things. Now a mountain is but a fist-sized stone; yet in its breadth and greatness, plants and trees grow upon it, birds and beasts dwell upon it, and precious deposits arise within it. Now water is but a spoonful; yet in its unfathomable depths, giant turtles, alligators, dragons, fish, and soft-shelled turtles live, and valuable resources multiply.”

Huang Deyuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “This composition is clear and cleanly written, and worthy of selection. It develops its argument through pointing to a single part and presenting the whole, and finally unifies them through sincerity alone. This amply demonstrates the care devoted to learning concerned with the fundamentals…”

In discussing the work of creation and transformation in bringing things into being, some statements refer to a single part, while others address the whole. To speak of a single part is to speak of something exceedingly small; to address the whole is to speak of something exceedingly great. When the great worthy speaks of this, what could surpass his elucidation of the workings of creation and transformation?

Now, that which arches above is Heaven. Heaven does not become vast through accumulation. If one speaks only of a single part, it is merely a patch of brightness; but when one addresses its entirety, it is boundless. The sun and moon display their forms, attached to it so as to shine down; the stars and constellations appear brightly, set upon it in dense arrays. Of all the myriad things, there is not one that it does not cover.

That which lies low beneath is Earth. Earth does not become vast through accumulation. If one speaks only of a single part, it is merely a handful of soil; but when one addresses its entirety, it is broad and deep. What rises aloft as Mount Hua, it bears without feeling its weight; what flows as rivers and seas, it holds without letting it leak away. Of all the myriad things, there is not one that it does not support.

As for a mountain’s breadth and greatness, these likewise do not come about through accumulation. To point to a single part is to speak of no more than a fist-sized stone; but when it comes to its entirety…

藏無不興於此矣水之不測亦非由積累而後爾也

知其功用足以化育乎萬物而不知所以化育乎萬

體之廣大也，草木於是乎生，禽獸於是乎居，凡其寶藏無不興於此矣。水之不測，亦非由積累而後爾也，指其一處，特一勺之多而已；及其全體之不測也，黿鼉、蛟龍、魚鼈之屬於此乎生，凡其貨財無不殖於此矣。噫！天也，地也，人徒知其功用足以覆載乎萬物，而不知所以覆載萬物者，本乎此誠也；山也，川也，人徒知其功用足以化育乎萬物，而不知所以化育乎萬物者，亦本乎此誠也。誠乎！誠乎！其造化所以為造化乎！苟無是誠，則造化之理或幾乎息矣，其何以致功用而極其盛哉？子思子言此，其所以發明造化之妙，無餘蘊矣。

易
「益，動而巽，日進无疆。天施地生，其益无方。凡益之道，與時偕行。」
戴昂
同考試官編脩趙批：題本無難，作者多不先言卦德成益之意，往往以天地聖人立說，殊失本旨。此篇融會傳義，辭理俱優，表而出之。
translation_en:
…entire body in its vastness, grass and trees grow upon it, birds and beasts dwell upon it, and all precious treasures without exception arise there. As for the unfathomability of water, neither does it become so only through gradual accumulation. Point to a single spot, and it is no more than a scoopful; yet when we speak of its entire body in its unfathomability, giant turtles, alligators, flood-dragons, dragons, fishes, and soft-shelled turtles are born within it, and all manner of goods and wealth without exception multiply there.

Ah! Heaven and Earth—people merely know that their functioning suffices to shelter and bear the myriad things, yet do not know that whereby they shelter and bear the myriad things is rooted in this sincerity. Mountains and streams—people merely know that their functioning suffices to transform and nourish the myriad things, yet do not know that whereby they transform and nourish the myriad things is likewise rooted in this sincerity. Sincerity! O sincerity! Is it not that whereby the creative transformation of nature is what it is? Were it not for this sincerity, the principle of creative transformation would almost cease; how then could it achieve its functioning and reach the pinnacle of its flourishing? In speaking thus, Master Zisi has elucidated the subtleties of creative transformation without leaving anything unexpressed.

Book of Changes (Yi)
"Increase (Yi): movement and遜 [gentle penetration], advancing daily without bound. Heaven bestows and Earth brings forth; its increase is without limit. Every way of increase proceeds in harmony with the time."
Dai Ang 戴昂
Comment (pi) by Associate Examiner and Historiographer (Bianxiu) Zhao: The topic itself presents no difficulty, yet most candidates fail to state first the meaning of how the virtues of the hexagram constitute Increase, often framing their arguments instead around Heaven, Earth, and the Sage, which quite misses the original purport. This essay thoroughly integrates the commentaries and meanings; both its diction and its reasoning are superior, so I single it out for distinction.

text:
考試官侍講杜批理明詞贍剖析無遺宜寘前列
考試官學士高批此篇講益之道理明而辞贍可謂
能發易之義者
動順於理而益無窮造化聖人同一自然之理而已
夫動而順理者益之道也造化運自然之理而萬物
受其益聖人體自然之理而天下受其益然則益道
之大造化聖人之益豈不與之同其大乎且夫益之
為卦下體震也震以一陽生於二陰之下有動之義
焉上體巽也巽以一陰伏於二陽之下有順之義焉
蓋順而不動則无以致益動而不順亦无以成益今
也巽上震下震動巽順動順於理此益之所以日進
不已廣大而无疆焉卦之為益如此而造化聖人之
益為何如哉是故自造化而觀之確然而位乎上者
天也隤然而位乎下者地也天氣下降萬物資之以
為始地氣上行萬物資之以為生凡兩間之物囿於
氣者以氣遂囿於形者以形成洪纎高下各正性命
而不偏飛潜動植保合大和而不失大以成大富有
而无外小以成小日新而不窮非造化之益為无方

天也隤然而位乎下者地也天氣下降萬物資之以
爲始地氣上行萬物資之以爲生凡兩間之物囿於
氣者以氣遂圎於形者以形成洪纖髙下各正性命
而不偏飛潛動立保合大和而不失大以成大富有
而无外小以成小日新而不窮非造化之益爲无方
punctuated:
考試官侍講杜批：理明詞贍，剖析無遺，宜寘前列。
考試官學士高批：此篇講益之道，理明而辞贍，可謂能發《易》之義者。
動順於理而益無窮，造化聖人同一自然之理而已。夫動而順理者，益之道也。造化運自然之理，而萬物受其益；聖人體自然之理，而天下受其益。然則益道之大，造化、聖人之益豈不與之同其大乎？且夫益之為卦，下體震也，震以一陽生於二陰之下，有動之義焉；上體巽也，巽以一陰伏於二陽之下，有順之義焉。蓋順而不動則无以致益，動而不順亦无以成益。今也巽上震下，震動巽順，動順於理，此益之所以日進不已、廣大而无疆焉。卦之為益如此，而造化、聖人之益為何如哉？是故自造化而觀之，確然而位乎上者，天也；隤然而位乎下者，地也。天氣下降，萬物資之以為始；地氣上行，萬物資之以為生。凡兩間之物，囿於氣者以氣遂，囿於形者以形成。洪纎高下，各正性命而不偏；飛潜動植，保合大和而不失。大以成大，富有而无外；小以成小，日新而不窮。非造化之益為无方

Comment by Examiner Du, Expositor-in-Waiting: The reasoning is clear and the diction is rich; the analysis leaves nothing out. It deserves to be placed in the front ranks.
Comment by Examiner Gao, Academician: This essay explains the Way of Increase (Yi) with clear reasoning and rich diction; it can truly be said to bring out the meaning of the Book of Changes (Yi).
When movement accords with principle, increase is inexhaustible; the creative transformation of nature and the sage share one and the same natural principle, and nothing more. Now, moving in accordance with principle is the Way of Increase. Creative transformation operates by natural principle, and the myriad things receive its benefit; the sage embodies natural principle, and the world receives his benefit. This being so, in the greatness of the Way of Increase, are not the benefits of creative transformation and of the sage equally great? Moreover, as a hexagram, Increase has Zhen (Thunder) as its lower trigram: Zhen, with one yang line arising beneath two yin lines, carries the meaning of movement; it has Xun (Wind/Gentleness) as its upper trigram: Xun, with one yin line crouching beneath two yang lines, carries the meaning of compliance. Indeed, if one is compliant yet does not move, there is no way to bring about benefit; if one moves yet is not compliant, there is likewise no way to accomplish benefit. Now, with Xun above and Zhen below, Zhen moves and Xun complies—moving in compliance with principle. This is why Increase advances daily without cease, vast and boundless. Such is Increase in the hexagram; what, then, of the benefits of creative transformation and of the sage? Therefore, viewed from the perspective of creative transformation: that which stands firm and is positioned above is Heaven; that which is yielding and is positioned below is Earth. As the vital energy of Heaven descends, the myriad things rely upon it for their beginning; as the vital energy of Earth ascends, the myriad things rely upon it for their birth. Among all things between Heaven and Earth, those bounded by vital energy achieve fulfillment through vital energy, and those bounded by form achieve completion through form. Great and small, high and low, each rectifies its nature and destiny without partiality; creatures that fly, dive, move, and grow as plants preserve in union the Great Harmony without loss. The great are brought to completion as great, abundant in possession and with nothing outside them; the small are brought to completion as small, daily renewed and inexhaustible. Is this not the benefit of creative transformation being without limit…

乎？夫所以如是者，一動順之理也。自聖人而觀之，財成輔相者，聖人之責也；仁民愛物者，聖人之心也。神道設教，必因時以厚民生；制器尚象，必隨時以利民用。凡益天下之道，不先時而有為，不後時而不為。如結繩不可以為治，則變而為書契；草木不可以衣被，則變而為衣裳。通其變，使民不倦；神而化之，使民宜之。何莫而非與時偕行之道乎？夫所以如是者，亦一動順之理也。愚故曰：動順於理而益無窮，造化聖人同一自然之理者，良以此歟！抑嘗考之，卦辭曰：「利有攸往，利涉大川。」文王之所係也。吾夫子從而彖之，既以卦體釋卦名義，復以卦體卦象釋卦辭，至此又以造化聖人極言而賛其大，益之道於是无餘蘊矣。不特此也，卦合震巽二體而成，有風雷相益之象。君子體之，求益於己者，亦唯遷善改過而已。益於人者，无大於是。不然，大象何以曰：「風雷，益。君子以見善則遷，有過則改。」

剛柔者，立本者也；變通者，趣時者也；吉凶者，貞勝者也；天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明
translation_en:
…is it not? What makes this so is the single principle of acting in accord with principle. Viewed in terms of the sage, regulating and completing the work of Heaven and Earth, and assisting their operations, are the sage’s responsibilities; benevolence toward the people and love for all things are the sage’s intentions. In establishing instruction through the numinous Way, he necessarily responds to the times to enrich the people’s livelihood; in making implements by taking the images as his models, he necessarily follows the times to provide useful things for the people. In every means of benefiting the world, he neither acts before the proper time nor leaves action undone after the time has come. Thus, when knotted cords can no longer serve to govern, he changes them to written documents; when grasses and trees can no longer provide covering, he changes them to upper and lower garments. He carries changes through so that the people do not grow weary; through numinous transformation, he enables the people to find what suits them. Which of these is not a way of advancing together with the times? What makes this so is likewise the single principle of acting in accord with principle. Thus I venture to say: action that accords with principle brings inexhaustible increase. Surely this is why the creative transformations of nature and the sage share the same principle of natural spontaneity!

I have also examined the hexagram statement: “It is beneficial to have somewhere to go; it is beneficial to cross the great river.” These are the words King Wen appended. Our Master Confucius subsequently composed the Commentary on the Judgment. He first used the hexagram’s structure to explain the meaning of its name, then used its structure and images to explain its statement. Here he further expounded its greatness to the fullest through the creative transformations of nature and the sage, praising it until nothing of the Way of Increase remained unexplored. Nor is this all. The hexagram is formed by combining the two trigrams Zhen and Xun, presenting the image of wind and thunder increasing one another. The gentleman embodies this: in seeking to improve himself, he need only turn toward goodness and correct his faults. Nothing is greater than this in bringing benefit to others. Otherwise, why does the Commentary on the Great Image say: “Wind and thunder: Increase. The gentleman accordingly turns toward goodness when he sees it, and corrects his faults when he has them”?

The firm and the yielding establish the foundation; change and continuity accord with the times; good fortune and misfortune prevail through constancy. The Way of Heaven and Earth is constantly displayed; the Way of the sun and moon is constant in its brightness…

即易書之體用，以見人事之占常相勝；即造化之正常，以明天下之理常有定。夫剛柔立本者，易之體；變通趣時者，易之用。而吉凶之占，造化人事之理，同一正常而已，夫豈有異哉？何則？乾之六畫為剛，而百九十二之陽爻皆剛也；坤之六畫為柔，而百九十二之陰爻皆柔也。雖有遠近中正之不同，承乘比應之不齊，然一剛一柔，各有定體，非剛柔者立本之謂乎？老陽之九變而通於少陰之八，則剛有時而趣於柔也；老陰之六變而通於少陽之七，則柔有時而趣於剛
translation_en:
…are so. All movement under Heaven is constant in the One.

Hu Hao 胡皞.

Associate Examiner Jiang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This topic has many threads. Other papers recite the words but lose their savor, with successes and failures in equal measure. This essay alone expounds and connects everything without omission: its author has grasped the subtleties in his heart. Who could say that it is inappropriate to single it out for distinction?”

Examiner Du, Expositor, comments: “By discussing the transformation of old yang into young yin, it clarifies how the firm and yielding accord with the time. It surpasses the other compositions.”

Examiner Gao, Academician, comments: “This essay elucidates the firm and yielding, transformation and continuity, comprehensively treating both the workings of creation and human affairs. It deserves to be singled out for distinction.”

By examining the substance and functioning of the Book of Changes, we see how, in prognostications concerning human affairs, one outcome invariably prevails over the other. By examining the correctness and constancy of creation, we understand that the principles governing all under Heaven always have a fixed basis. The firm and yielding, which establish the foundation, constitute the substance of the Changes; transformation and continuity, which accord with the time, constitute its functioning. Prognostications of good and ill fortune, and the principles of creation and human affairs, share the same correctness and constancy. How could they differ?

Why is this so? The six lines of Qian are firm, and all one hundred and ninety-two yang lines are firm. The six lines of Kun are yielding, and all one hundred and ninety-two yin lines are yielding. Although they differ in being distant or near, central or correctly placed, and vary in their relationships of supporting, riding upon, adjacency, and correspondence, each firm line and each yielding line has its fixed constitution. Is this not what is meant by saying that the firm and yielding establish the foundation?

When the nine of old yang transforms and passes into the eight of young yin, the firm accords with the time by tending toward the yielding. When the six of old yin transforms and passes into the seven of young yang, the yielding accords with the time by tending toward the firm…

punctuated: 也。雖剛不能一於剛，柔不能一於柔，然自此而彼，變以從時，非變通者趣時之謂乎？剛柔以卦言，而卦之辭有吉凶之殊；變通以爻言，而爻之辭有休咎之異。順理則吉，而吉常勝夫凶，凶與吉不兩立也；逆理則凶，而凶常勝夫吉，吉與凶不並行也。觀於造化人事，可見矣。夫天以至健之體，常示人以易；地以至順之體，常示人以簡。雖心不能以不愆，陽不能以不伏，而貞觀之理常自若□。日為陽精而明乎晝，月為陰精而明乎夜，雖中不能以不昃，盈不能以不蝕，而貞明之理常自若也。天下之事，紛紜交錯，不可以一端求；天下之動，進退存亡，不可以一例測。然而順理則裕，從欲惟危，同一揆也；惠迪之吉，從逆之凶，无二致也。是則造化人事之正常，即吉凶之貞勝；而吉凶貞勝之占，又即卦爻之辭也。豈可以二而求之哉？抑考易之為書，辭、變、象、占四者而已。上文曰「八卦成列」，以象言也；曰「剛柔相推」，以變言也；曰「係辞而命之」，以辞言也；至此曰「吉凶貞勝」，則又以占而言也。吁！君子居則觀象玩辞，動則觀變玩占，此章盡之矣。學易者考諸
translation_en:
…so it is. Although the firm cannot remain exclusively firm, nor the yielding exclusively yielding, they pass from one state to the other, changing to accord with the time. Is this not what is meant by saying that change and continuity follow the time? Firmness and yielding are spoken of in terms of the hexagrams, whose statements distinguish good fortune from misfortune; change and continuity are spoken of in terms of the lines, whose statements distinguish favorable from unfavorable outcomes. Following principle brings good fortune, and good fortune invariably prevails over misfortune: misfortune and good fortune cannot both stand. Opposing principle brings misfortune, and misfortune invariably prevails over good fortune: good fortune and misfortune do not proceed together. This can be seen by observing the processes of creation and human affairs.

Heaven, through its supremely vigorous constitution, constantly reveals ease to humanity; earth, through its supremely compliant constitution, constantly reveals simplicity to humanity. Although the heart cannot avoid going astray [?], and yang cannot avoid lying concealed, the principle of their constant manifestation remains unchanged [illegible character]. The sun is the essence of yang and illuminates the day; the moon is the essence of yin and illuminates the night. Although the sun at its zenith cannot avoid declining, and the full moon cannot avoid being eclipsed, the principle of their constant illumination remains unchanged. The affairs of the world are tangled and interwoven and cannot be understood from a single aspect. The movements of the world—advancing and retreating, enduring and perishing—cannot be gauged by a single rule. Nevertheless, following principle brings abundance, while following desire brings peril: the same standard applies throughout. The good fortune of following the Way and the misfortune of following what opposes it admit of no discrepancy.

Thus, the regular and constant order of creation and human affairs is precisely the constant alternation in the ascendancy of good fortune and misfortune; and the prognostications of this ascendancy are precisely the statements attached to the hexagrams and lines. How could these be investigated as two separate things? Moreover, if we examine the Changes as a book, it comprises only four things: statements, changes, images, and prognostications. The preceding text says, “The eight trigrams are arranged in order”: this speaks of images. It says, “The firm and the yielding impel one another”: this speaks of changes. It says, “Statements are attached to pronounce upon them”: this speaks of statements. Here it says, “Good fortune and misfortune constantly prevail in turn”: this, again, speaks of prognostication. Ah! At rest, the gentleman observes the images and ponders the statements; when acting, he observes the changes and ponders the prognostications. This chapter encompasses it all. Let those who study the Changes examine…

書
三載考績三考黜陟幽明庶績咸熙分北三苗
李英
同考試官侍講徐批經義之作所以明理貴乎辭
足以達而已奚以新奇為哉連日閱卷作者固多
然非冗則巧令人厭之此卷七篇純潔如一
不巧不冗而考績一題於主意尤有發明故
表而出之
考試官侍講杜批詞理皆優可取
===
考試官學士高批此篇於考課分北之旨講貫
甚明故錄之以為式
聖君因時考課之法明而信故衆功皆廣而遠人得
以别也盖法之明而效之大者理勢之必然也聖世
考課之法既極其明又豈不足以致衆功之廣而遠
人之區别哉昔者帝舜於命二十二人之後立為考
課之法以時而舉行之所以察其能敬亮天工與否
也故三載者天運三周時物三變而人之功過有可
見矣於是考其功而課其殿最覈其實而第其上下

translation_en:
Classic of Documents (Shu)

"Every three years there was an examination of achievements; after three examinations, the undeserving were demoted and the deserving promoted. Thus all achievements were broadly resplendent, and the Sanmiao were divided and separated."

Li Ying 李英

Associate Examiner, Expositor-in-waiting Xu 徐 comments: The composition of essays on the meaning of the Classics is meant to elucidate principle; what is valued is simply that the words suffice to convey the meaning—what need is there for novelty and eccentricity? Reading papers over several consecutive days, there were certainly many skilled writers, yet where they were not verbose they were overly artful, making one weary of them. The seven essays in this paper are uniformly pure and lucid, neither overly artful nor verbose, and this essay on the topic of examining achievements particularly brings out the main idea; therefore I single it out for distinction.

Examiner, Expositor-in-waiting Du 杜 comments: Both diction and reasoning are superior; it is worthy of selection.

Examiner, Academician Gao 高 comments: This essay expounds the import of performance evaluation and the division and separation [of the Sanmiao] very clearly; therefore we record it to serve as a model.

Because the sage ruler's method of timely performance evaluation was clear and trustworthy, all achievements were broadened and distant peoples could be differentiated. Indeed, when a method is clear, its effects are great—this is the inevitable course of principle and circumstance. Since the method of performance evaluation in that sage age reached the utmost clarity, how could it fail to bring about the broadening of all achievements and the differentiation of distant peoples? In antiquity, after Emperor Shun 舜 appointed the twenty-two men, he established the method of performance evaluation and carried it out at regular intervals, as the means to observe whether or not they were able reverently to aid the work of Heaven. Now in three years, the heavenly cycle completes three revolutions and the seasonal things undergo three transformations, so that men's merits and faults become visible. Thereupon he examined their achievements and graded their lowest and highest ratings, verifying the reality of their performance and ranking them from top to bottom…

title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
焉然未可遽施以黜陟也必遲而至于三考以施之
盖三考則歷乎九載而時之久也功以久而可見人
以久而可知彼其有職業不脩幽而無功者則削地
貶爵以黜之才美外見明而有功者則加地進律以
陟之執此之政堅如金石行此之令信如四時則考
課之法明而信也為何如哉由是掌教掌刑者教敷
而刑措典禮典樂者禮備而樂和平水土者有告厥
成功之美播百穀者有烝民乃粒之休治功其有不
廣者乎不特此也三苗之衆昔也頑不即工今則得
===
以分而背之向也負固不服今則得以區而别之善
者以留不善者以去聖人立心之仁處事之義兩盡
其道遠人其有不服者乎吁考課之法莫善於有虞
之世而考課之效亦莫盛於有虞之世也大抵人臣
之任事不可無考課之法人君之立法要必得寛猛
之宜此所以考績於三載而黜陟三考為盡善盡美
也厥後成周訓迪厥官冢宰歲終受會詔廢置三歲
則計治行黜賞與有虞不同者所謂帝王之治因時
損益故也說者謂太和在虞周之世豈無所自而然哉

===

則計治行黜賞與有虞不同者所謂帝王之治因時
損益故也說者謂太和在虞周之世豈無所自而然哉
punctuated: 焉。然未可遽施以黜陟也，必遲而至于三考以施之。盖三考則歷乎九載而時之久也，功以久而可見，人以久而可知。彼其有職業不脩、幽而無功者，則削地貶爵以黜之；才美外見、明而有功者，則加地進律以陟之。執此之政堅如金石，行此之令信如四時，則考課之法明而信也為何如哉！由是掌教掌刑者，教敷而刑措；典禮典樂者，禮備而樂和；平水土者，有告厥成功之美；播百穀者，有烝民乃粒之休。治功其有不廣者乎？不特此也，三苗之衆，昔也頑不即工，今則得以分而背之；向也負固不服，今則得以區而别之。善者以留，不善者以去，聖人立心之仁、處事之義，兩盡其道，遠人其有不服者乎？吁！考課之法莫善於有虞之世，而考課之效亦莫盛於有虞之世也。大抵人臣之任事，不可無考課之法；人君之立法，要必得寛猛之宜。此所以考績於三載，而黜陟三考，為盡善盡美也。厥後成周訓迪厥官，冢宰歲終受會詔廢置，三歲則計治行黜賞，與有虞不同者，所謂帝王之治因時損益故也。說者謂太和在虞周之世，豈無所自而然哉！
translation_en: …therein. Yet one must not precipitately apply demotions and promotions; one must wait until three evaluations have elapsed before applying them. For three evaluations span nine years, which is a long period of time; achievements become visible through time, and men become known through time. Those who fail to cultivate their duties, remaining obscure and without achievement, are demoted by having their lands reduced and their ranks lowered; those whose talents and virtues manifest outwardly, proving illustrious and accomplished, are promoted by having their lands increased and their ceremonial standing advanced. Holding to this governance as firmly as metal and stone, and enforcing these ordinances as reliably as the four seasons—how supremely clear and trustworthy is this method of personnel evaluation! Consequently, under those in charge of education and punishments, moral instruction was spread and punishments were set aside; under those directing rites and music, rituals were made complete and music harmonious; he who regulated the waters and land achieved the splendor of reporting his completed work; and he who sowed the hundred grains brought about the blessing of the multitude having grain to eat. Could the achievements of governance fail to be broad and far-reaching? Not only this: as for the host of the Three Miao (Sanmiao), formerly they were obstinate and refused to come to their tasks, whereas now they could be divided and isolated; previously they relied on their strongholds and refused to submit, whereas now they could be sorted and distinguished. The good were retained and the evil removed; the sage’s benevolence in establishing his mind and his righteousness in handling affairs both fulfilled their proper Way—could distant peoples fail to submit? Ah! The method of personnel evaluation was never more perfected than in the age of Yu [Shun], and the efficacy of personnel evaluation never more flourishing than in the age of Yu! In general, when ministers undertake their duties, there cannot be an absence of evaluation laws; and when a ruler establishes laws, he must attain the proper balance between leniency and strictness. This is why examining achievements every three years and carrying out demotions and promotions after three evaluations was utterly good and utterly admirable. Thereafter, when flourishing Zhou instructed and guided its officials, the Grand宰 (zhongzai, Minister of State) received the accounts at the end of each year to advise the throne on dismissals and appointments, and every three years audited administrative performance to carry out demotions and rewards. That this differed from the practice of Yu was because the governance of emperors and kings adapts to the times by subtracting and adding. Commentators say that Supreme Harmony prevailed in the ages of Yu and Zhou—how could this have come about without cause!

title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
公既定宅伻来来視予卜休恒吉我二人共貞
公其以予萬億年敬天之休
岳正
同考試官教諭林批此成王授使者復周公定洛告
卜之詞其曰恒吉曰天休實主於卜洛定洛而言此卷
得之且遣詞蒼古迥出諸作况後二場亦称本房
幾四百卷未有能出其右者擢居魁選孰曰不宜
考試官侍講杜批洛誥一題場中作者於共貞敬天之
休多窘略殊無發明此作詞理優贍筆力老成
===
必深於經學者髙薦無忝
考試官學士髙批此篇善形容成周君臣膺卜之
吉敬天之休佳作也
賢君之荅大臣既述其卜洛而同當上天之徵必祈
其宅洛而永保上天之眷盖洛邑之定既有以徵諸
天命矣洛邑既成豈不足以壽夫天命哉思昔成王
當洛邑既定之日復周公獻卜之使意其若曰周公
於澗瀍之間河洛之表既卜王城而定周家之基業
又卜下都而為殷民之所居於是馳駟牡之車走一

===
賢君之眷大臣既述其卜洛而同當上天之徵必祈
其宅洛而永保上天之眷蓋洛邑之定既有以徵諸
天命矣洛邑既成豈不足以壽夫天命哉思昔成王
當洛邑既定之日復周公獻卜之使意其若曰周公
於澗瀍之間河洛之表既卜王城而定周家之基業
又卜下都而為殷民之所居於是馳駟牡之車走一
punctuated:
「公既定宅，伻来，来視予卜休恒吉。我二人共貞，公其以予萬億年敬天之休。」
岳正
同考試官教諭林批：此成王授使者復周公定洛告卜之詞。其曰「恒吉」、曰「天休」，實主於卜洛、定洛而言。此卷得之，且遣詞蒼古，迥出諸作，况後二場亦称。本房幾四百卷，未有能出其右者，擢居魁選，孰曰不宜？
考試官侍講杜批：《洛誥》一題，場中作者於「共貞」、「敬天之休」，多窘略殊無發明。此作詞理優贍，筆力老成，必深於經學者，髙薦無忝。
考試官學士髙批：此篇善形容成周君臣膺卜之吉、敬天之休，佳作也。
賢君之荅大臣，既述其卜洛而同當上天之徵，必祈其宅洛而永保上天之眷。盖洛邑之定，既有以徵諸天命矣；洛邑既成，豈不足以壽夫天命哉？思昔成王當洛邑既定之日，復周公獻卜之使，意其若曰：周公於澗、瀍之間，河、洛之表，既卜王城而定周家之基業，又卜下都而為殷民之所居，於是馳駟牡之車，走一
translation_en:
"The Duke having fixed the settlement, sent a messenger to come and show me the auspicious and ever-fortunate divinations. We two shall jointly bear the responsibility; may the Duke with me for tens of thousands and hundreds of millions of years revere the grace of Heaven."
Yue Zheng 岳正
Associate Examiner Instructor Lin 林 comments: These are the words King Cheng 成王 gave to the messenger in reply to the Duke of Zhou 周公 reporting the divinations upon fixing the capital at Luo 洛. When it speaks of "ever-fortunate" and "the grace of Heaven," it truly centers on divining for Luo and fixing the settlement at Luo. This paper has grasped this; moreover, its diction is vigorous and ancient, far surpassing the other compositions, and the papers of his latter two sessions are also commendable. Among the nearly four hundred papers in this examination ward, none can surpass it. Promoting it to the top rank—who would say that is inappropriate?
Examiner Expositor-in-Waiting Du 杜 comments: On this topic from the "Announcement concerning Luo" (Luo gao 洛誥), candidates in the examination hall mostly wrote in a cramped and cursory manner regarding "jointly bear the responsibility" and "revere the grace of Heaven," without any real elucidation. This composition is rich in expression and reasoning, and mature in brushwork. He must be one deeply versed in the study of the Classics; he is wholly worthy of high recommendation.
Examiner Academician Gao 高 comments: This essay excels at depicting how the ruler and minister of thriving Zhou received the auspiciousness of the divination and revered the grace of Heaven. It is a fine piece of work.
When a worthy ruler replies to his great minister, having recounted how his divining for Luo allows them jointly to bear the auspicious signs of High Heaven, he must pray that his settling in Luo will forever preserve the favor of High Heaven. Indeed, the fixing of the settlement of Luo already served to verify the Mandate of Heaven; once the settlement of Luo is completed, how could it not suffice to prolong the Mandate of Heaven? Thinking back to the day when the settlement of Luo had been fixed, King Cheng replied to the messenger sent by the Duke of Zhou to present the divinations, his meaning being to the following effect: Between the Jian 澗 and Chan 瀍 rivers, and beyond the Yellow River and the Luo River, the Duke of Zhou first divined the site of the Royal City (Wangcheng 王城) to establish the foundational enterprise of the House of Zhou, and further divined the site of the Lower Capital (Xiadu 下都) to serve as the dwelling place for the people of Yin 殷. title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
介之使視我以所卜之休美我固有以當其美矣公
也實與國家而同其休戚宜亦有以共當是美焉視
我以龜兆之恒吉我固有以膺是吉矣公也實與王
室而相為始終宜亦有以同膺是吉焉况乎營建新
都創作大邑偉乎前朝後市之傑制煥然左祖右社
之宏規制度鼎新規模弘遠不惟今日可以承天而
治民雖萬有千歲之遠為子孫者亦得以據形勝而
制方来也不惟今日可以繼天而出治雖億萬斯年
之久為子孫者亦得以守其要會而朝天下也公其
===
以予萬億年敬天之休者如此其忠愛之心為何如
哉抑洛邑之作周公相視其始召公經營其成盖欲
成王宅中圖治承天以治民也今也成王之復公既
曰公不敢不敬天之休来相宅又曰公其以予萬億
年敬天之休其所以倚重於公也至矣而公之愛王
則曰萬年厭于乃德又曰王伻殷乃承叙萬年其永
觀朕子懷德其所以望於君也切矣吁周之歴世三
十卜年八百而過其數者豈非洛邑匹休之驗成王
周公敬天之所致也歟

punctuated:
介之使，視我以所卜之休美，我固有以當其美矣；公也實與國家而同其休戚，宜亦有以共當是美焉。視我以龜兆之恒吉，我固有以膺是吉矣；公也實與王室而相為始終，宜亦有以同膺是吉焉。况乎營建新都，創作大邑，偉乎前朝後市之傑制，煥然左祖右社之宏規。制度鼎新，規模弘遠。不惟今日可以承天而治民，雖萬有千歲之遠，為子孫者亦得以據形勝而制方来也；不惟今日可以繼天而出治，雖億萬斯年之久，為子孫者亦得以守其要會而朝天下也。公其以予萬億年敬天之休者如此，其忠愛之心為何如哉！」
抑洛邑之作，周公相視其始，召公經營其成，盖欲成王宅中圖治，承天以治民也。今也成王之復公，既曰「公不敢不敬天之休，来相宅」，又曰「公其以予萬億年敬天之休」，其所以倚重於公也至矣；而公之愛王，則曰「萬年厭于乃德」，又曰「王伻殷乃承叙萬年，其永觀朕子懷德」，其所以望於君也切矣。吁！周之歴世三十、卜年八百而過其數者，豈非洛邑匹休之驗，成王、周公敬天之所致也歟！
translation_en:
…single envoy to show me the auspicious beauty of the divinations. I indeed have that whereby to receive this beauty; yet you, O Duke, truly share the joys and sorrows of the state, so it is fitting that you should also jointly receive this beauty. You show me the constant auspiciousness of the tortoise-shell omens. I indeed have that whereby to embrace this auspiciousness; yet you, O Duke, truly see things through from beginning to end with the royal house, so it is fitting that you should also jointly embrace this auspiciousness. Moreover, in constructing the new capital and founding the great city—how magnificent is the outstanding arrangement of the court in front and the market behind, and how resplendent is the grand design of the ancestral temple on the left and the altars of soil and grain on the right! The institutions are newly established, and the scale is vast and far-reaching. Not only today can we thereby uphold Heaven and govern the people, but even across the distance of ten thousand and a thousand years, those who are our descendants will also be able to rely on its strategic terrain to control the future. Not only today can we thereby succeed to Heaven and issue governance, but even through the duration of a hundred million and ten thousand years, those who are our descendants will also be able to guard its vital hub and receive the homage of all under Heaven. That you, O Duke, would have me for ten thousand and a hundred million years revere the grace of Heaven in such a manner—how profound is your heart of loyalty and affection!"

Furthermore, in the building of the city of Luo, the Duke of Zhou (Zhou Gong 周公) inspected its site at the beginning, and the Duke of Shao (Shao Gong 召公) planned and managed its completion, for they wished King Cheng (Cheng Wang 成王) to dwell at the center to plan his governance, upholding Heaven in order to rule the people. Now, in King Cheng's reply to the Duke, he first says, "The Duke did not dare not to revere the grace of Heaven, and came to inspect the site for a residence," and again says, "May the Duke enable me for ten thousand and a hundred million years to revere the grace of Heaven"—that whereby he relied heavily upon the Duke was supreme indeed! And in the Duke's affection for the King, he says, "For ten thousand years may they beimbued with your virtue," and again says, "May the King cause the Yin people to receive the regular order for ten thousand years, so that they forever observe my children and cherish their virtue"—that whereby he placed his hopes in his ruler was earnest indeed! Ah! That the Zhou dynasty lasted for thirty generations and divined a duration of eight hundred years—and even exceeded that number—was this not the verification of the city of Luo matching Heaven's grace, and the result of King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou revering Heaven?

text:
詩
戎車既安如輊如軒四牡既佶既佶且閑薄伐
玁狁至于大原文武吉甫萬邦為憲
李尚
同考試官侍講謝批此篇說出尹吉甫不逞服遠之
威為諸侯之法深合本旨超出衆作可謂有識之
士髙薦何忝
考試官侍講杜批明潔典則非淺學可到也
考試官學士髙批文字善於鋪叙可觀
===

諸侯之法哉昔者宣王命尹吉甫以伐玁狁有功而
歸詩人作此以美之想夫吉甫之行也車之駕則安
閑矣視其前後又皆如輊如軒而適其宜焉殆不異

則強盛矣視其驅馳又皆既佶且閑而中節焉殆不

translation_en:
Classic of Poetry (Shijing): "The war chariots were steady, balanced alike before and behind; the four-stallion teams were robust, both robust and well-trained. We drove off the Xianyun, as far as Taiyuan. Civil and martial is Jifu, a model to all the states."

Li Shang 李尚

Comment by Associate Examiner and Expositor-in-Waiting Xie 謝: This essay brings out how Yin Jifu 尹吉甫 did not indulge his might in subjugating the distant, thereby serving as a model for the feudal lords. It deeply accords with the original meaning of the text and surpasses the crowd of other compositions. He may truly be called a scholar of insight—what shame is there in recommending him for a high rank!
Comment by Examiner and Expositor-in-Waiting Du 杜: Clear, pure, and canonical in standard; this is not something that shallow learning could attain.
Comment by Examiner and Academician Gao 高: The writing is skilled in its exposition and well worth reading.

When military array is magnificent yet one does not indulge in the might of subjugating the distant, the commander's virtue is complete and suffices to serve as a model for the feudal lords. Now, subjugating the distant certainly values a magnificent military array, but setting a model lies even more in the completeness of the commander's virtue. Had his military array not been magnificent and his commander's virtue not been complete, how then could he have achieved the merit of subjugating the distant and become a model for the feudal lords? In ancient times, King Xuan 宣王 commanded Yin Jifu to attack the Xianyun; when he returned with merit, the poet composed these lines to praise him. Imagine Jifu setting forth on the march: the yoking of his chariots was steady and composed, and whether viewed from the front or from the rear, they were balanced as if tilting forward or rising behind, each suited to its proper measure—hardly different from "forth go the chariots rumbling, thefalcon-banners and tortoise-banners gleaming," which was why the chariots were so well-balanced. The driving of his horses was vigorous and strong, and when observed at the gallop, they were both robust and well-trained, keeping to the rhythm—hardly distinct from "the four stallions were long and broad, huge and large-headed," which was why the horses were so well-drilled. title: 正統十三年會試錄
text:
習之馬而駕適調之車則軍容之盛可知矣彼玁狁
匪茹侵鎬及方在吉甫選鋒進銳聲其罪而致討焉
固其宜也使他人處此孰不欲是伐是肆以遂摧枯
拉朽之勢是致是附以覬執訊獲醜之功而吉甫則
但盡境而還內不失乎王師之仁逐出之而已外不
失乎禦戎之道此其不逞服遠之威所以為文武吉
甫也是故守先王治夷狄之法而不窮追信乎其為
文若所謂其風肆好以贈申伯特緒餘耳却玁狁而
奏膚大之功以定王國信乎其為武若所謂有嚴有
===
翼共武之服誠不誣耳文既足以附眾武又足以威
敵則將德之全可見矣凡天下之諸侯欲附眾而得
人心者非法吉甫之文不可也欲養威而敵王愾者
非法吉甫之武亦不可也文武之德雖全於吉甫之
身而儀刑之施則及於萬邦之廣詩人於成功之日
不惟叙其平玁狁之功而復称其為諸侯之法非深
知吉甫其能然哉抑考是詩六章首章至四章則言
戎裝之整飭將帥之嚴敬此章則言治戎狄之道車
馬安閑驅之出境不窮追也卒章則言休兵飲至樂

translation_en: … well-trained horses to draw well-balanced chariots, the splendor of the military array can be known. Those Xianyun "did not measure their own strength," "invading Hao and Fang." For Yin Jifu 尹吉甫 to select his vanguard and advance his elite troops, proclaiming their crimes and executing punitive expedition against them, was certainly fitting. Had someone else been in this position, who would not have wished "to attack them and to assail them" so as to carry through the momentum of crushing dry twigs and pulling up rotten wood, and "to bring them and to attach them" so as to covet the merit of "seizing prisoners for questioning and capturing the crowd of captives"? Yet Jifu merely reached the border and returned, inwardly not losing the benevolence of the King's army; he simply drove them out and stopped, outwardly not losing the proper way of defending against the Rong barbarians. This refusal to indulge in the might of subjugating the distant is why he is called "the civil and martial Jifu." Therefore, upholding the former kings' method of governing the Yi and Di barbarians and not pursuing them to the bitter end—truly this is his civility; as for what is called "its air is grand and fine" in the ode presented to the Earl of Shen 申伯, that is merely a byproduct. Repelling the Xianyun and achieving great merit to stabilize the royal kingdom—truly this is his martiality; as for what is called "solemn and reverent, attending to the affair of war," it is truly no false praise. Since his civility was sufficient to attach the multitude and his martiality was also sufficient to overawe the enemy, the completeness of a commander's virtue can be seen. Among all the feudal lords under Heaven, any who wish to attach the multitude and win the hearts of the people cannot do so without taking Jifu's civility as their model; any who wish to cultivate majesty and withstand those whom the King hates cannot do so without taking Jifu's martiality as their model either. Although civil and martial virtues were complete in Jifu's own person, the reach of his exemplary model extended across the breadth of the myriad states. On the day of his success, the poet not only recounted his merit in pacifying the Xianyun, but also praised him as a model for the feudal lords—without knowing Jifu deeply, how could he have done so? Moreover, if we examine the six stanzas of this ode: from the first stanza to the fourth stanza, it speaks of the orderly preparation of military equipment and the solemn reverence of the commander; this stanza speaks of the way of dealing with the Rong and Di barbarians, with chariots and horses calm and unhurried, driving them out of the border without pursuing them to the end; the final stanza speaks of resting the troops and drinking upon returning to the ancestral temple, rejoicing…

text:

中興之盛豈不於斯而可見乎
自今以始歲其有君子有穀詒孫子于胥樂兮

「自今以始，歲其有。君子有穀，詒孫子。于胥樂兮。」

萬安

同考試官脩撰裴批：此篇文詞雅贍，允當時之善頌善禱者。
考試官侍講杜批：形容燕飲胥樂氣象，宛然在目，可取。
考試官學士高批：此篇得詩人頌禱之意。

魯人之頌禱其君，既欲其豐年之始於今，又欲其善道之傳於後，此其所以為可樂也。夫國家之樂，莫大乎屢豐年之祥，尤莫大乎傳善道於後。今魯人以是而頌禱其君，願望之意為何如哉！夫國以民為本，民以食為天。苟民食不足，幾何不至於艱食乎？今焉惟願自今以始，自始及終，陰陽和而風雨時，多黍多稂，亦有高廩，非惟今歲之若然，而來歲亦無不然也；自天降康，豐年穰穰，非惟一歲之如此，而屢歲亦無不如此也。如是則民食自足，而國本亦固矣。以是頌禱之，亦云至矣，而魯人之意猶以為未也。故又以為君
translation_en:
… sharing the banquet's joy with filial and brotherly men, then any inclination toward exhausting the military and engaging in reckless warfare disappears. Can the flourishing of King Xuan's restoration not be seen right here?

"From this time forth, may the years be abundant. May the lord have goodness to bequeath to his grandsons and sons. Together they rejoice!" [Book of Odes, Lu Song, "Youbi"]

Wan An 萬安

Associate Examiner and Senior Compiler (xiuzhuan) Pei comments: The diction of this essay is elegant and rich; it truly matches those of antiquity who excelled at eulogy and prayer.
Examiner and Expositor-in-Waiting (shijiang) Du comments: It depicts the atmosphere of feasting and mutual rejoicing so vividly that it seems right before one's eyes; worthy of selection.
Examiner and Academician (xueshi) Gao comments: This essay captures the poet's intent in praising and praying.

When the people of Lu praised and prayed for their lord, they wished both that abundant years would begin from the present and that the way of goodness would be transmitted to posterity; this is why it was cause for rejoicing. Now, the joy of a state has nothing greater than the auspiciousness of repeated abundant harvests, and even more so, nothing greater than transmitting the way of goodness to posterity. Now that the people of Lu praise and pray for their ruler with this, how deep is their earnest hope! For the state takes the people as its foundation, and the people take food as their heaven. If the people's food is insufficient, how long before they fall into destitution of food? Here they only wish that beginning from now, from start to finish, yin and yang may be in harmony and wind and rain timely, with abundant millet and abundant rice [reading 秔 for 稂], and tall granaries as well—not only that this year be so, but that the coming year be no different; that peace be sent down from Heaven, with abundant years in profusion—not only that a single year be like this, but that repeated years all be like this as well. If it is so, then the people's food will naturally suffice, and the foundation of the state will also be secure. 之子孫乃所以承宗祀者也苟無善以詒傳之幾何
不至於乖戾舊章而殄厥宗祀乎兹焉惟願君之至
善見於言行者無悖繆之失而足以為子孫之軌範
而子孫莫不是則而是倣也見於政事者無駁雜之
弊而足以為子孫之儀刑而子孫莫不是訓而是式
也如此則子孫皆善而庶幾不殄厥宗祀矣夫豐年
之屢獲則有以為生民之計此其有可樂也善道之
傳後則有以為子孫之計此其又可樂也以可樂之
事頌禱於燕飲之間其必爰笑爰語懽忻之意形於

之子孫乃所以承宗祀者也。苟無善以詒傳之，幾何不至於乖戾舊章而殄厥宗祀乎？兹焉惟願君之至善，見於言行者無悖繆之失，而足以為子孫之軌範，而子孫莫不是則而是倣也；見於政事者無駁雜之弊，而足以為子孫之儀刑，而子孫莫不是訓而是式也。如此則子孫皆善，而庶幾不殄厥宗祀矣。夫豐年之屢獲，則有以為生民之計，此其有可樂也；善道之傳後，則有以為子孫之計，此其又可樂也。以可樂之事頌禱於燕飲之間，其必爰笑爰語，懽忻之意形於酬酢之際；或歌或咢，豫樂之情著於交接之時。其相與燕樂之意何其至哉！吁！於燕飲之頃而致頌禱之辭，於願望之餘而致勸勉之意，魯之僖公何其得人心之至如此乎！雖然，魯人之頌禱僖公不止於此也。《泮水》則頌其克廣德心，有以屈此群醜而獲夫多福；《閟宫》則頌其興衰起廢，有以懷乎隣國而順乎萬民也。後之欲知僖公之賢者，可不合三詩而觀之哉！

translation_en:
… the lord's descendants are the ones who carry on the ancestral sacrifices. If there is no goodness to bequeath and pass down to them, how long before they violate the old statutes and cut off their ancestral sacrifices? Thus they only wish that the lord's supreme goodness, as manifested in his words and deeds, be free from perverse or erroneous faults and suffice to serve as a standard for his descendants, so that none of his descendants fail to take it as their rule and model; and that as manifested in his governance, it be free from impure or mixed abuses and suffice to serve as a pattern for his descendants, so that none of his descendants fail to take it as their instruction and formula. If it is like this, then his descendants will all be good, and perhaps they will not cut off their ancestral sacrifices. Now, when abundant years are repeatedly reaped, there is the means to provide for the livelihood of the people—this is something in which one can rejoice. When the good Way is transmitted to posterity, there is the means to provide for one's descendants—this is also something in which one can rejoice. Offering praises and prayers for such joyful things amidst banqueting and drinking, they will surely laugh and converse, with feelings of delight appearing as toasts are exchanged; they will sing and beat drums, with sentiments of pleasure and joy manifest as they mingle together. How utmost is the spirit of their mutual feasting and rejoicing! Ah! To offer words of praise and prayer during a moment of feasting and drinking, and to convey an intent of encouragement and exhortation beyond their wishes and hopes—how did Duke Xi of Lu win the hearts of the people to such an utmost degree as this! Even so, the people of Lu's praises and prayers for Duke Xi did not stop here. In "The Semicircular Water" (Panshui), they praised his ability to broaden his virtuous heart, whereby he subdued the crowd of evil ones and obtained manifold blessings; in "The Secluded Temple" (Bigong), they praised his reviving the declined and raising the neglected, whereby he cherished the neighboring states and brought harmony to the myriad people. Those of later times who wish to know the worthiness of Duke Xi—how can they not bring the three odes together and examine them!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

為事一旦乘潰蔡之勢為伐楚之舉厚集之陣當其
前掎角之師擬於後以此衆戰誰能禦之而桓公乃
見不尓宣賜履之言於大伐之日徵包茅之貢於次

罪甘心以徼同好之歡雍容壇坫牲歃以盟而楚人
自是不敢抗衡鄭人之患息矣桓公之功為何如哉

以楚師

陳外懼之戒聽用其言誰曰不可而厲公之計不然

translation_en:
… [expelling Chu] as his business. Once he capitalized on the momentum of routing Cai to launch the campaign against Chu, with heavily massed formations confronting them in front and pincer forces poised in the rear—fighting with such a host, who could withstand him? Yet Duke Huan's view was not thus. He proclaimed the words concerning the territories granted for campaigning on the day of the great expedition, and demanded the tribute of wrapped rush-grass after halting at Xing. Consequently, the people of Chu were struck with terror, and Qu Wan graciously came, bowing his head to submit to the guilt of failing to send tribute, and gladly seeking the goodwill of mutual friendship, conducting the ceremonies with poised dignity at the covenant altar and smearing the blood of the sacrificial victim to seal the alliance. From then on, the people of Chu did not dare to contend as equals, and the troubles of the people of Zheng ceased. How great indeed was the merit of Duke Huan! This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) commends him.

As for the middle of the Spring and Autumn period, the power of Chu grew arrogant again; this year with the army of Chu [? text missing in original] … had been for a long time, and the vacillation of Zheng was extreme. Duke Li of Jin succeeded to the hegemony; emboldened by the victories at Jiaogang and Masui, not a day passed that he did not set his mind on repelling Chu and subduing Zheng. Now, on account of punishing Zheng, he raised an army and fought the Battle of Yanling. At that time, Luan Shu offered the counsel of fortifying the ramparts, and Wenzi [Fan Wenzi 范文子] set forth the warning about external threats; had he listened to and employed their words, who would have said it was wrong? Yet Duke Li's calculation was not so. Relying on the victory of a single arrow shot by Lü Qi, he brought about the rout of the two armies of Chu and Zheng—thus this victory was merely a matter of luck. Moreover, Duke Li ultimately lacked the virtue to sustain victory and repeatedly raised armies to attack Zheng: not stopping after one campaign, he attacked a second time; not stopping after a second campaign, he attacked a third time. At first he drew in Viscount Shan (Shanzi 單子) to go with him, and in the end he coerced Yin and Shan to march together, rushing about on the roads and indulging in the force of arms. From then on, the people of Zheng did not submit, and the people of Chu grew ever more arrogant. How great, then, was the failure of Duke Li! This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals criticizes him.

Alas! In the beginning, Duke Huan of Qi attacked Chu, and the enterprise of founding the hegemony thereby…

公之得失昭昭然矣抑考屈完來盟而服包茅之貢
則王命申於遠夷者桓之功也與師服鄭而假尹單
之威則王命不行於貳國者厲之罪也二伯之功罪
係於王命之行否此春秋所以深致其意歟
取濟西田〔僖三十一〕齊人取濟西田〔宣元〕齊人歸我
濟西田〔宣十〕取汶陽田〔成二〕晉侯使韓穿來言汶
陽之田歸之于齊〔成八〕齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰
田〔定十〕
彭時

===

考試官學士高　批〔叙事明而辭順可取〕
地利始有得失而終定於大國之私地利縱有得失
而終定於聖人之化蓋濟西汶陽之得失雖有不同
然歸而由於私恩者孰若歸於聖化之為正哉思昔
西周之盛王道流行分茅胙土而土田之屬乎列國
punctuated:
盛；終也，晋厲戰楚，而服貳之威徒假。《春秋》備書，而二公之得失昭昭然矣。抑考屈完來盟，而服包茅之貢，則王命申於遠夷者，桓之功也；興師服鄭，而假尹、單之威，則王命不行於貳國者，厲之罪也。二伯之功罪，係於王命之行否，此《春秋》所以深致其意歟！

地利始有得失，而終定於大國之私；地利繼有得失，而終定於聖人之化。蓋濟西、汶陽之得失雖有不同，然歸而由於私惠者，孰若歸於聖化之為正哉！思昔西周之盛，王道流行，分茅胙土，而土田之属乎列國
translation_en:
… flourished; in the end, Duke Li of Jin (Jin Li) fought Chu, yet the authority to subdue a duplicitous state was merely borrowed. The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records all of this in full, and the successes and failures of the two dukes are made crystal clear. Moreover, if we examine how Qu Wan came to make a covenant and submitted to the tribute of wrapped rush-grass, then the extension of the royal mandate to distant barbarians was the merit of Duke Huan; whereas in raising armies to subdue Zheng and borrowing the authority of Yin and Shan, the failure of the royal mandate to prevail over a duplicitous state was the offense of Duke Li. The merits and offenses of the two hegemons hinged upon whether or not the royal mandate was carried out—is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals conveyed its meaning so profoundly here?

"We took the fields west of the Ji" [Thirty-first year of Duke Xi]; "Men of Qi took the fields west of the Ji" [First year of Duke Xuan]; "Men of Qi returned to us the fields west of the Ji" [Tenth year of Duke Xuan]; "We took the fields of Wenyang" [Second year of Duke Cheng]; "The Marquis of Jin sent Han Chuan to come to speak about the fields of Wenyang, and we returned them to Qi" [Eighth year of Duke Cheng]; "Men of Qi came to return the fields of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin" [Tenth year of Duke Ding].

Peng Shi 彭時
